description: A safety officer must authorize and control a weekend internal cleaning of a shared blending vessel before the next production campaign, with input from maintenance, quality, production planning, and industrial hygiene.

shared_context.S1: Blending Vessel 4 is scheduled for internal cleaning this weekend before the next production campaign.
shared_context.S2: Elena makes the final decision on whether personnel may enter the vessel and what controls are required.
shared_context.S3: The vessel is isolated from normal production service, and the plant's routine confined-space entry procedure applies.
shared_context.S4: Before authorizing the work, Elena conducts the plant's standard review with maintenance, quality, production planning, and industrial hygiene.
shared_context.S5: The weekend work package covers the vessel's entry prerequisites, required controls, and production release deadline.
shared_context.S6: During this standard review, each specialist gives a concise statement of any confirmed requirement in their area; after all four area statements are heard, Elena records a conditional authorization with the disclosed prerequisites and controls and settles the review.
shared_context.S7: The review decides the entry controls and work-package commitments; it does not wait for cleaning-duration or laboratory-turnaround estimates that are outside this review.

PF1.text: Raj's maintenance inspection found that the vessel's lower drain actuator must be replaced before entry; the replacement takes exactly 3 hours, and the vessel has four separate energy-isolation points that must be locked out. He recorded the finding in a pending maintenance note that has not yet been entered in the central work-order system.

PF2.text: Mina's review of the campaign change found that the previous batch was an allergen-containing formulation; quality requires exactly three documented rinse samples and a quality hold until all three pass before the vessel can be released. She completed the review in the batch file, which has not yet been attached to the weekend work package.

PF3.text: Caleb confirmed with the customer scheduling desk that the next campaign must begin Monday at 06:00, so the vessel must be released by Sunday at 18:00 to preserve the production sequence. The confirmation is in his scheduling email but has not yet been copied into the maintenance calendar.

PF4.text: Tori's industrial-hygiene review identified the cleaning residue as a respiratory sensitizer; entry therefore requires supplied-air respirators and continuous atmospheric monitoring throughout the entry. Her report is awaiting final sign-off and is not yet posted at the vessel.

acceptance_conditions: Entry must be authorized with all listed prerequisites and controls.
The entry plan must be recorded as a controlled or conditional confined-space plan with the listed prerequisites and controls.
The lower drain actuator must be replaced before entry, requiring exactly 3 hours of maintenance downtime.
All four vessel energy-isolation points must be locked out.
Exactly three rinse samples must be documented.
The vessel must remain on quality hold until all three rinse samples pass.
The vessel must be released by Sunday at 18:00.
Supplied-air respirators must be required for entry.
Continuous atmospheric monitoring must be required throughout entry.
The respiratory hazard basis must be recorded as the cleaning residue being a respiratory sensitizer.
Maintenance, sanitation validation, production release, and atmospheric-monitoring commitments must be recorded.
The sensitizer finding must be cited in the justification.

content_checks.C2: decisions['entry_plan_type'] in ['conditional_with_prerequisites', 'controlled confined-space entry with enhanced controls', 'standard confined-space entry with enhanced IH controls', 'controlled confined-space entry with supplied-air respirators and continuous atmospheric monitoring', 'confined-space entry with supplied-air respirators and continuous atmospheric monitoring']
content_checks.C11: any((c['type'] in ['actuator_replacement_and_lockout', 'maintenance', 'control', 'lockout_verification', 'documentation'] and c['target'] in ['Raj', 'raj', 'maintenance', 'all', 'All', 'ALL']) for c in commitments) and any((c['type'] in ['sanitation_validation', 'quality', 'control', 'quality_release', 'documentation'] and c['target'] in ['Mina', 'mina', 'quality', 'all', 'All', 'ALL']) for c in commitments) and any((c['type'] in ['production_release_schedule', 'production_planning', 'scheduling', 'control', 'documentation'] and c['target'] in ['Caleb', 'caleb', 'production planning', 'all', 'All', 'ALL']) for c in commitments) and any((c['type'] in ['atmospheric_monitoring', 'industrial_hygiene', 'entry_controls', 'control', 'documentation'] and c['target'] in ['Tori', 'tori', 'industrial hygiene', 'all', 'All', 'ALL']) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The maintenance finding changes the plan to require actuator replacement with exactly 3 hours of downtime and lockout of exactly four isolation points.
The allergen history changes sanitation verification to exactly three rinse samples and requires the quality hold to remain until all three pass.
The customer confirmation changes the production plan to require release by the exact deadline of Sunday 18:00.

The sensitizer finding changes authorization to a controlled or conditional plan requiring supplied-air respirators and continuous monitoring, and changes the recorded hazard basis to the cleaning residue being a respiratory sensitizer.
